newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indocement spinoff aim to focus on cement.
newsitem.headline: Indocement spinoff aim to focus on cement.

text.p: PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa said on Tuesday its proposal to sell its 50.1 percent stake in PT Indofood Sukses Makmur was aimed to focusing on its core business in the cement industry.

"Though the company remains convinced that Indofood will continue to expand and prosper, management has decided to refocus the company's efforts on the burgeoning growth of the cement business, particularly in Indonesia," the firm said.
Indocement said in a statement it had proposed a spinoff and sale of its 50.1 percent shareholding in Indofood to shareholders and to a new purchaser.

The proposed spinoff is expected to be effected by the distribution of 724.34 million Indofood shares representing 39.56 percent of Indofood share capital to shareholders of Indocement in the form of special dividend.
The company said it will also sell 193.10 million Indofood shares, representing 10.54 percent of the company, to private firms controlled by Indonesia's Sampoerna family.
Food maker QAF Limited said in a statement on Tuesday it had agreed to acquire a majority stake in Indofood.
Indocement, Indofood and QAF are controlled the Salim Group, Indonesia's largest conglomerate.

Salim group CEO Anthony Salim said this restructuring was another step in the Salim group's streamlining that began with the sale of Bogasari to Indofood in 1995 and continued with the sale of the related food businesses to Indofood in March this year.
"These efforts clearly demonstrate the group's desire to concentrate its core business into separate entities," Salim said in the statement.

"Segregating Indofood from Indocement will not only improve the ability of the investing public to better understand the business of the separate entities but will also allow the management of the companies to focus directly on each company's respective operations and core competencies," he added.
Indocement said the company now intends to strengthen its current leading market position while leveraging its competitive advantage as the industry's lowest-cost cement maker.
"A portion of the proceeds from the proposed sale of its 10.54 percent shareholding in Indofood will be used to repay debt," Indocement said.
In addition, the company also plans to make further investments to expand its domestic cement distribution and logistics capabilities while considering cement investment opportunities in the region.
"In principal, this de-merger is good for Indocement but the timing is not good," an analyst with foreign securities firm said.

The analyst said the positive point of the move is that now investors can valuate Indocement purely as a cement company, but he predicted Indonesia would face a cement oversupply in 1999 and this would reflect negatively on Indocement.
On Tuesday, Indocement made strong gains rising 250 rupiah to close at 4,800 rupiah after the sale plan was announced.
"The market is overreacting to the news, that is why its shares price rose so sharply," the analyst said.
He added that a fair price for Indocement was about 3,800 rupiah after it was given a 25 percent premium price compared with other local cement firms such as Semen Gresik or Semen Cibinong.
